hypothesis: For the same breeding SiteIDs, later recolonization occurs at a higher surrounding population state than earlier abandonment, beyond generic temporal structure in the observed parent trajectories.

observed_estimand.transition_state: mean of the two annual censuses bracketing the transition

hierarchy: mean repeated spells within species x physical MasterSite x SiteID
mean SiteIDs within species x physical MasterSite

primary_gate_1.test: one-sided sign-flip of species-level mean H

primary_gate_2.name: noncircular_common_shift_null
primary_gate_2.rule: For each shift group, draw one integer shift uniformly from its Stage-B-frozen eligible_common_shifts and apply that same shift to every spell in the group. No wrap. Keep the observed multivariate abundance matrices fixed.

confirmatory_support: Both primary gates must pass. Neither can rescue failure of the other.
boundaries: Support establishes event-aligned, history-dependent spatial recovery at the measured SiteID scale, not a unique Allee/social mechanism.
The common-shift null controls generic phase/trajectory effects without circular wrap but is not a complete generative occupancy model.
Same-site pairing controls fixed site identity; time-varying habitat remains possible.
stop_rule: After SMP magnitude opening, do not change H, transform, hierarchy, shift groups, eligible shifts, null family, simulation count, taxon subset, or support thresholds.
